q.t: Name the open strings from thickest to thinnest.
o: E A D G B E
E B G D A E
A B C D E F
E A D G C E
q.e: Every Amateur Does Get Better Eventually: E A D G B E.

q.t: Which string is string number 1?
q.e: String 1 is the highest-sounding string — the thin one nearest the floor.

q.t: Which string is string number 6?
q.e: String 6 is the lowest-sounding, thickest string.

q.t: Which finger is finger 1?
q.e: Index 1, middle 2, ring 3, little 4. The thumb is T.

q.t: Which finger is finger 4?
q.e: Index 1, middle 2, ring 3, little 4.

q.t: Each fret raises the note by…
q.e: Fret to fret is always one half step.

q.t: Where should you press the string?
o: On top of the metal fret
In the middle between two frets
q.e: Just behind the fret needs the least pressure and doesn't buzz.

q.t: Which fret has the double dot?
q.e: The double dot marks the 12th fret — the octave.

q.t: What note is the 12th fret of the A string?
q.e: Fret 12 is one octave above the open string, so it has the same name: A.

q.t: Where does your thumb go on the fretting hand?
o: On the front of the frets
q.e: The thumb sits behind the neck, roughly behind your middle finger, so the fingers can curve over.

q.t: What note is fret 1 of the low E string?
q.e: E to F is only a half step, so fret 1 is F.

q.t: What note is fret 3 of the low E string?
What note is fret 5 of the low E string?
q.e: E, F, F♯, G, G♯, A — fret 5 is A.

q.t: What note is fret 2 of the A string?
What note is fret 3 of the A string?
q.e: A → A♯ (1) → B (2) → C (3). B to C is one fret.

q.t: What note is fret 1 of the B string?
q.e: B to C is a half step, so fret 1 is C.

q.t: What note is fret 3 of the B string?
Why do the frets get closer together further up the neck?
o: Each one shortens a shorter string by the same fraction
To make room for the pickups
So that the high frets sound louder
q.e: Each fret shortens the string by the same fraction for one half step. A fraction of a shorter string is a smaller distance.

q.t: Why do musicians call the thin string 'string 1'?
q.e: Strings are numbered from the highest note, so the thin high e is string 1.

q.t: Why should your fingers be curved, pressing with the tips?
o: A flat finger would mute the next string
So the thumb can reach the strings
q.e: A curved finger touches only its own string. A flat one lies across the next string and stops it ringing.

q.t: What note is fret 3 of the D string?
q.e: D → D♯ (1) → E (2) → F (3). E to F is one fret.

q.t: What note is fret 2 of the G string?
What note is fret 7 of the low E string?
q.e: E F F♯ G G♯ A A♯ B — fret 7 is B.

q.t: What note is fret 8 of the low E string?
q.e: Fret 7 is B, and B to C is one fret, so fret 8 is C.

q.t: What note is fret 5 of the A string?
q.e: A A♯ B C C♯ D — fret 5 is D, the same as the open D string.

q.t: Fret 5 of the low E string sounds the same as which open string?
q.e: E up 5 half steps is A — the next string.

q.t: Fret 5 of the D string sounds the same as which open string?
q.e: D D♯ E F F♯ G — 5 half steps up is G, the next string.

q.t: To match the open B string, which fret of the G string do you press?
q.e: G → B is only 4 half steps (G G♯ A A♯ B), so it is the 4th fret, not the 5th.

q.t: On the A string, which fret gives G?
q.e: A A♯ B C C♯ D D♯ E F F♯ G — G is 10 half steps up.

q.t: Fret 13 of a string gives the same note name as…
q.e: From fret 12 the pattern starts again, one octave up. So fret 13 = fret 1 + 12.

q.t: What note is fret 6 of the B string?
q.e: B C C♯ D D♯ E F — fret 6 is F.

q.t: What note is fret 4 of the D string?
q.e: D D♯ E F F♯ — fret 4 is F♯.

q.t: What note is fret 7 of the G string?
q.e: G G♯ A A♯ B C C♯ D — fret 7 is D.

q.t: On the low E string, which fret gives D?
q.e: Fret 8 is C, fret 9 is C♯, fret 10 is D.

q.t: On the high e string, which fret gives the note G?
q.e: The high e has the same notes as the low E: E F F♯ G — fret 3.

q.t: What note is fret 15 of the low E string?
q.e: 15 − 12 = 3, and fret 3 of the E string is G.

q.t: Most strings are tuned 5 half steps apart. Which neighbours are only 4 apart?
q.e: G → B is G♯, A, A♯, B = 4 half steps. All the other neighbours are 5.

q.t: You have no tuner but the low E is right. How do you tune the A string?
o: Match it to fret 5 of the low E
Match it to fret 12 of the low E
Match it to fret 4 of the low E
Match it to the open low E
q.e: Fret 5 of the low E is A, so the open A string should sound exactly the same.

q.t: Which note appears on the low E string at fret 1 and on the D string at fret 3?
q.e: Low E fret 1 = F. D string: D D♯ E F — fret 3 = F.

q.t: Why is it easier for a beginner to play the spider at frets 5–8 than at frets 1–4?
q.e: Frets get closer together up the neck, so four fingers reach four frets without a big stretch.
